• We landed we found a crowd of merchants and clients eager (2) ________ business with us. This line shows that the when they landed they come to know that the merchants were eagar
 
• Here, we need Infinitive to complete the meaning of the sentence.
 
• Do is the root form of the Main Verb
 
• To do is the To+ Infinitive.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****

 
• ** ****Do is the main verb here**.

 
 
• "We" is the subject of the sentence and it is followed by the Main Verb **Found**
 
• According to the grammatical structure, we can not use only do.
 
• **So option 1 is the wrong answer**.
 
 
 
• "**Doing" **is a Present Participle form of Main Verb (Do)
 
 
• Present Participle form is preceded by helping verbs such as ""**am/is/are/was/were/have been/ has been/ had been/ shall be / will be / shall have been/ will have been"**
 
• In Present Continuous, Past Continuous, Future Continuous, Present perfect continuous, Past perfect continuous, Future perfect continuous tense.

• **So option 4 is the wrong answer.**
 
 
 
• **Use of Infinitives.**
 
 
• **​**An infinitive is a verbal, verb form or construction that plays the role of a different part of speech in a sentence.
 
• Although infinitives contain verbs, they cannot function as verbs.
 
• They do not convey a sense of tense on their own, and sentences containing them must include at least

 one finite main verb. 
 
• Infinitives are formed by placing **to in front of the base form of a verb**.
 
• They are negated by placing not in front of them.

• Thus, the current situation has (5)________ many boys and girls and they are waiting for things to get back to normal.
 
• Let's see the meanings of the given words-
 
 
• **​supported- **to agree with and give encouragement to someone or something because you want him, her, or it to succeed
 
• **encouraged- **to make someone more likely to do something, or to make something more likely to happen
 
• **discourage- **to make someone feel less confident, enthusiastic, and positive about something, or less willing to do something
 
• **upset- **to make someone worried, unhappy, or angry
 
 
 
• The speaker says that the current situation is so worse that many boys and girls are disheartened or get upset and think that when things get back to normal.

**So the correct passage will be:-** *Many reports have said that in the context (1) of Covid-19 lockdown, schooling, and college education are likely to be online. The reports have (2) also pointed out that this change will deny the students the experience of studying in a physical (3) campus. Thus, the current situation has **(5) upset** many boys and girls and they are waiting for things to get back to normal.*

subject: ENG
question: What is the significance of animal imagery in The Thought Fox?

options.text: It gives a bright picture of the countryside, not connected to the theme of creativity
It highlights the anxiety of the poet in regard to nature and its unpredictability
It points out the drawbacks of industrialization in relation to nature and its inhabitants.
It hides the abstract idea of poetic inspiration under a visible, palatable metaphor

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 4: It hides the abstract idea of poetic inspiration under a visible, palatable metaphor.***

 
 
• The passage explicitly states that **"the symbolism of poetic inspiration is concealed behind the animal imagery."**
 
• Poetic inspiration is an **abstract** concept (something that cannot be seen or touched). By using the **fox** as a metaphor, Ted Hughes makes this abstract process **visible** and **palatable** (easier to understand or digest) for the reader.
 
• The "part-by-part" description of the fox (nose, eyes, prints) serves as a physical representation of how a poem gradually takes shape in the mind.
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: It gives a bright picture of the countryside...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage confirms that the imagery is directly **"symbolic of the process of poetic inspiration,"** contradicting the idea that it is not connected to the theme of creativity.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: It highlights the anxiety of the poet in regard to nature...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. While there is a sense of "loneliness" mentioned, it is a **creative loneliness** (the absence of ideas), not an anxiety about the unpredictability of nature itself.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: It points out the drawbacks of industrialization...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage does not discuss industrialization, factories, or environmental drawbacks. It focuses entirely on **literary composition**.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Metaphor vs. Symbol**: A metaphor directly compares two unlike things. Here, the fox *is* the thought. As a symbol, the fox represents the wild, untameable, and sudden nature of a **creative spark**.
 
• **Animal Poetry**: Ted Hughes is known as an "animal poet." He often used animals to bridge the gap between the **human intellect** and the **instinctual world**.
 
• **The "Internal" Forest**: In the poem, the setting is both a literal dark night and a metaphorical "forest" of the poet's mind where the "Thought Fox" lives.

subject: ENG
question: What central argument does Wollstonecraft make in A Vindication of the Rights of Woman?

options.text: Women ought to recognize their inferior position as a natural obligation and therefore should not dispute the current social order.
Women's education is a necessity for their active and equal participation in society, thus overthrowing the male-dominated social structure.
Women are by nature fit for the house and should not engage in the intellect, as the quest for knowledge would disturb the social order.
The advancement of society is dependent on the confinement of women to domestic roles and the maintenance of the male-dominated structure.

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 2: Women's education is a necessity for their active and equal participation in society...***

 
 
• The passage explicitly identifies **education** as the core of Wollstonecraft's argument. It states she "sees education as the **only means** to enable women to participate in society."
 
• She argues that the "lack of education" is what "keeps women in a secondary position," rather than any natural deficiency. By advocating for education, she seeks to move women out of this "secondary position" within the **patriarchal set-up**.
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: Women ought to recognize their inferior position as a natural obligation...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The text says she **"rejects the conventional approach"** that categorized women as naturally weak and inferior. She views their status as a result of social conditions (lack of education), not nature.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Women are by nature fit for the house and should not engage in the intellect...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. Wollstonecraft's entire thesis, as described in the passage, is a **critique** of this very idea. She believed women should have the same intellectual opportunities as men to contribute to society.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: The advancement of society is dependent on the confinement of women...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. Wollstonecraft argues that women play a "crucial role in shaping a society" specifically through their active **participation** and education, not through confinement.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vindication**: This word means the action of clearing someone of blame or suspicion, or proof that someone or something is right/justified. Wollstonecraft is "justifying" why women deserve the same rights as men.
 
• **Secondary Position**: In social theory, this refers to a group that is marginalized or has less power, autonomy, and status compared to the dominant group (in this case, men in a patriarchy).
 
• **Rationality**: A key part of her argument (implied by the rejection of "weakness") was that women are **rational beings** capable of reason, and therefore education is their birthright.
 
• **The Role of Mothers**: While she advocated for societal participation, she also argued that educated mothers would better raise the next generation of citizens, making women's education beneficial for the whole of society.

__

• It further explains that she **"stressed the importance of education"** as the **"only means"** to allow women to participate in society and move out of their "secondary position," which aligns with the idea of contesting their current status.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Women are naturally inferior and should be limited to domestic responsibilities...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage explicitly states that Wollstonecraft **"rejects the conventional approach, which categorised women as naturally weak and inferior to men."**
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Gender inequality is so entrenched that it cannot be addressed through social reform...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. Wollstonecraft’s entire philosophy is built on the hope of **social reform through education**. She believed the "lack of education" was the cause, meaning providing it would be the solution.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: Intellectual pursuits for women only result in family discord...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. Far from causing discord, she argued that education would make women **more effective** in their roles, specifically in "shaping a society through their participation in bringing up children."
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subjugation**: This term refers to the action of bringing someone or something under wide control or domination. Wollstonecraft's critique focuses on how women were socialized to view this control as a "natural" state.
 
• **Proto-feminism**: Since Wollstonecraft wrote in the 18th century, her ideas are "proto" (meaning "first" or "earliest") because they preceded the organized feminist movements of the 19th and 20th centuries.
 
• **The Role of Reason**: Wollstonecraft argued that because women possess the **same capacity for reason** as men, keeping them uneducated was an injustice to their humanity.

question: Which of the following best summarizes the main idea of the passage?

options.text: Spaceships are simple machines designed only by aerospace engineers.
The challenges faced by spaceship scientists are minimal due to advanced tech.
The development of spaceships is a complex, collaborative effort involving multiple scientific fields to overcome extraordinary challenges.
Human space exploration is limited and has not progressed due to difficulties.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To identify the **main idea**, we must look for the most comprehensive statement that reflects the entire content of the passage.
 
• The passage covers three main themes: 
 
 
• **Multidisciplinary Collaboration:** It details the "confluence of various scientific disciplines" such as aerospace engineering, astrophysics, and biology.
 
• **Extraordinary Challenges:** It lists "formidable obstacles" like the vacuum of space, radiation, zero gravity, and communication delays.
 
• **Human Achievement:** it describes the development as a "monumental testament" to "human ingenuity and perseverance."
 
 
 
• **Option 3** accurately captures all these elements: the complexity, the collaborative nature, the variety of fields, and the overcoming of significant challenges.
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 1:** This is **too narrow** and factually incorrect based on the text. The passage states spaceships are "intricate systems" (not simple) and involve multiple types of scientists, not just aerospace engineers.
 
• **Option 2:** This **contradicts** the text. The passage describes the challenges as "formidable" and "hostile," not minimal.
 
• **Option 4:** This is **false** according to the passage, which states that these efforts have "revolutionized our understanding" and are "pushing the very boundaries of human exploration."
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **3**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In high-level competitive exams, the main idea should never be too specific or too negative if the passage is generally positive. Look for "holistic" words like "complex," "collaborative," and "multidisciplinary" to find the strongest summary.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multidisciplinary:** Combining or involving several academic disciplines or professional specializations.
 
• **Monumental:** Great in importance, extent, or size.
 
• **Interstellar:** Situated or occurring between the stars.
 
• **Physiological:** Relating to the way in which a living organism or bodily part functions.

subject: ENG
question: What is the central difference between structuralism and post-structuralism in Barthes’s work?

options.text: Structuralism turns down language-based methods, while post-structuralism totally depends on the author’s life.
Structuralism seeks stable meaning, whereas post-structuralism accepts ambiguity and playfulness
Structuralism puts forward affective interpretation, whereas post-structuralism stimulates ethical readings.
Structuralism is concerned with spontaneous creativity, whereas post-structuralism prefers predetermined rules.

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Methodological vs. Random approach.***

 
 
• The passage contrasts Barthes's structuralist work as "detailed, methodological, and forbiddingly technical," which implies a search for **stable, systematic meaning**. In contrast, his post-structuralist work is described as "random comments" that emphasize the "randomness of the material."
 
 
 
• ***Fixed vs. Radical Independence.***
 
 
• Structuralism seeks to unify or limit a text through specific analysis. Post-structuralism, however, asserts a "radical textual independence," where the text is "free by its very nature" from restraints, accepting **ambiguity and the "play" of the text**.
 
 
 
• ***Rejection of Unified Meaning.***
 
 
• By "announcing the death of the author," Barthes moves away from the idea that a work can be "unified or limited" by a single intention, allowing for a multiplicity of meanings that characterize the post-structuralist phase.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: Incorrect because structuralism is heavily based on language methods, and post-structuralism specifically rejects the "author's life" as the source of meaning.
 
• **Option 3**: Incorrect because the passage does not discuss "affective interpretation" or "ethical readings" as the primary distinction between these two phases.
 
• **Option 4**: Incorrect because it reverses the definitions; structuralism is the one that uses "methodological" (predetermined) rules, while post-structuralism emphasizes the "randomness" and "freedom" of the text.

question: What marked Roland Barthes’s shift from structuralism to post-structuralism?

options.text: His gradual rejection of narrative theory and complete move into political writing.
His decision to limit his work to classical literature rather than contemporary writing.
The contrast between his technical structuralist essay “The Structural Analysis of Narrative” and the playful style of The Pleasure of the Text.
His adoption of psychological theories to explain literary meaning.

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Methodological Evolution.***

 
 
• The passage highlights Barthes's transition by contrasting his 1966 essay, which was "detailed, methodological, and forbiddingly technical," with his 1973 work, *The Pleasure of the Text*.
 
 
 
• ***The Shift to Randomness and Play.***
 
 
• Unlike his earlier structured approach, his later post-structuralist phase is marked by "random comments on narrative, arranged alphabetically," which purposefully emphasizes the randomness of the material over rigid systems.
 
 
 
• ***Textual Independence.***
 
 
• This shift represents a move toward "radical textual independence," where the text is seen as free from the restraints of authorial intention or strict methodological frameworks.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: Incorrect because the passage focuses on his shift within narrative theory and literary criticism, not a move into political writing.
 
• **Option 2**: Incorrect because the passage does not mention Barthes limiting himself to classical literature; it discusses his evolving approach to the nature of narrative itself.
 
• **Option 4**: Incorrect because the text attributes his shift to the "Death of the Author" and the independence of the text, rather than the adoption of psychological theories.

question: Why is The Thought Fox considered one of Hughes’ most celebrated early poems?

options.text: For the reason that it deals with the poet's intimate relations rather than his art in the making
Since the poem deals with the themes of the countryside and the industrialization of Northern Ireland
Due to the fact that it reveals the mystery of the creative process by means of abundant, vivid imagery

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 3: Due to the fact that it reveals the mystery of the creative process by means of abundant, vivid imagery.***

 
 
• The passage describes the poem as a **"perfect illustration"** of how poetic inspiration comes to a writer.
 
• It "reveals the mystery" by showing that inspiration is not a sudden, complete event but a **gradual process**, which Hughes captures through **"vivid imagery"** of the fox appearing part by part (nose, eyes, prints).
 
• The use of the fox as a symbol for **imaginative powers** is what makes the poem a celebrated early work.
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: For the reason that it deals with the poet's intimate relations...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage explicitly states that the poem is about **"the process of poetic inspiration"** (art in the making) rather than the poet's personal or intimate relationships.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Since the poem deals with the themes of the countryside and industrialization...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. While Ted Hughes often wrote about the countryside, this specific passage makes no mention of **industrialization** or Northern Ireland.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: As the poem does not use metaphors at all...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The text clarifies that the poem is **"symbolic"** and that the imagery **"conceals"** the meaning, which is the definition of metaphorical writing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

subject: ENG
question: What was the factor that contributed to Brecht's concept that performers ought to maintain a certain amount of detachment from their roles?

options.text: The realistic acting approach practiced by Stanislavsky
The spontaneous methods used in the Italian commedia dell'arte
The emotional truthfulness in Chekhov's plays
The significant movements of the Chinese theatre, where players do not completely identify with their character

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 4: The significant movements of the Chinese theatre, where players do not completely identify with their character.***

 
 
• The passage explicitly identifies this influence in the final sentence: **"This theatre also shows Chinese theatre influence, as the actors kept a distance from the characters they impersonated on stage."**
 
• This "distance" or detachment is a core component of Brecht's **"alienation effect,"** which aims to prevent the audience (and the performer) from becoming emotionally lost in the role.
 
• By maintaining this detachment, the performer acts as a **demonstrator** of the character's actions rather than "becoming" the character, allowing the audience to remain objective.
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: The realistic acting approach practiced by Stanislavsky.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage notes that Brecht's work gained recognition specifically because people were **"rejecting Stanislavsky-oriented realism."** Stanislavsky advocated for total identification with the character, which is the opposite of detachment.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: The spontaneous methods used in the Italian commedia dell'arte.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. While Brecht was influenced by many forms, **commedia dell'arte is not mentioned** in this passage as the source for his concept of performer detachment.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: The emotional truthfulness in Chekhov's plays.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. Chekhov’s plays are typically associated with the realism and emotional depth that Brecht sought to move away from in Epic Theatre. Furthermore, Chekhov is **not mentioned** in the text.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mei Lanfang**: Brecht was famously inspired by the Chinese opera singer Mei Lanfang. He observed that Chinese actors seemed to "watch themselves" while performing, which helped him formalize the idea that actors should stay emotionally separate from their roles.
 
• **The Fourth Wall**: In traditional realism, the "fourth wall" is never broken. In Brecht's Epic Theatre, influenced by these non-Western traditions, the actor frequently acknowledges the audience, effectively **shattering the illusion** of reality.
 
• **Alienation Effect (V-Effekt)**: The goal of this detachment is to turn the spectator into an **observer**. Instead of feeling *with* the character, the audience is encouraged to think *about* the character's choices and the social structures influencing them.

subject: ENG
question: Which of the following best distinguishes Epic Theatre from traditional realist drama?

options.text: It presents the story in an episodic manner and interacts with the audience directly to provoke their critical thinking
It seeks to encourage the audience's emotional release by making the illusion of reality more convincing.
It avoids addressing social issues and primarily explores internal psychological conflicts.
It emphasizes ornate sets and costumes specifically to heighten the illusion of reality.

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 1: It presents the story in an episodic manner and interacts with the audience directly to provoke their critical thinking.***

 
 
• The passage defines Epic Theatre as following an **"episodic structure,"** meaning scenes are not "tightly knit" but stand as individual units.
 
• It explicitly mentions that this form **"frequently broke the plot to talk to the spectators in a direct manner,"** using analysis and argument to provoke an objective conclusion.
 
• This is the core of Brecht's goal: to move from emotional empathy to **critical analysis**.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: It seeks to encourage the audience's emotional release...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. Emotional release (catharsis) is a hallmark of traditional drama. Brecht sought to **"dissuade the audience from empathizing"** to ensure they remained intellectually engaged.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: It avoids addressing social issues...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage describes Epic Theatre as **"instructive"** and **"didactic,"** which inherently involves teaching the audience about social, political, or moral issues.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: It emphasizes ornate sets and costumes...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The text states that Epic Theatre **"refrained from creating an illusion."** Ornate sets designed to heighten realism would contradict the **alienation effect**.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Episodic vs. Linear**: Traditional realist drama usually follows a linear path where each scene builds tension toward a climax. Epic Theatre is episodic, jumping between times or locations to keep the audience from getting "swept away" by the story.
 
• **The Spectator's Role**: In realist drama, the spectator is a passive observer. In Brecht's theory, the spectator is an **active participant** who must judge the events on stage.
 
• **Alienation Effect**: By using techniques that "alienate" or "estrange" the audience from the action, Brecht ensures that the stage remains a place for **intellectual inquiry** rather than just emotional escapism.

subject: ENG
question:
**Identify the voice of the sentence.**

"The narrative unfolds as characters seek to discover who committed the crime."
solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 3: Active voice***

 
 
• In the **active voice**, the subject of the sentence performs the action expressed by the verb.
 
• In the provided sentence, there are three clauses, all of which use the active voice: 
 
 
• **"The narrative unfolds"**: The subject (narrative) is performing the action of unfolding.
 
• **"characters seek"**: The subject (characters) is performing the action of seeking.
 
• **"who committed the crime"**: The subject (who) is performing the action of committing.
 
 
 
• Since the subjects are the "doers" of the actions and the verbs do not follow the "be + past participle" pattern, the sentence is in the active voice.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: Passive voice***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. In the passive voice, the subject receives the action (e.g., "The crime was committed by someone"). The sentence does not use this structure.
 
 
 
• ***Option 1 & 2: Causative and Reflexive voice***
 
 
• These are **incorrect**. The **causative voice** involves one person causing another to do something (e.g., "She had him discover the crime"). The **reflexive voice** involves a subject performing an action on itself (e.g., "The narrative unfolded itself"). Neither applies here.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Active Voice**: Focuses on the "doer." It is generally more direct, concise, and vigorous than the passive voice. (Example: *The detective solved the mystery.*)
 
• **Passive Voice**: Focuses on the "receiver" or the action itself. It is often used when the doer is unknown or less important. (Example: *The mystery was solved by the detective.*)
 
• **Middle Voice**: Sometimes, verbs like "unfold" or "open" are used in a way that is neither strictly active nor passive (e.g., "The door opened"). While linguistically distinct in some languages, in standard English grammar tests, "The narrative unfolds" is categorized under **Active Voice** because it lacks passive markers.

subject: ENG
question: How were The Movement writers often identified socially and culturally?

options.text: By their aristocratic background and preference for the elite salon
Through their working-class origins and radical political activism
Through their connection with cosmopolitan intellectual circles and experimental art
Through their middle-class roots, beer-drinking, and pipe-smoking habits

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 4: Through their middle-class roots, beer-drinking, and pipe-smoking habits.***

 
 
• **The Movement** writers were often identified with a distinctly **middle-class, provincial** background. They were frequently scholarship boys from grammar schools who felt alienated from the upper-class "metropolitan" elite.
 
• Culturally, they adopted a persona of the **"plain man."** This was famously symbolized by their preference for **beer and pipes** over the wine and experimental drugs associated with previous avant-garde or "Bohemian" circles.
 
• They took pride in being **anti-intellectual** in their public image—though they were highly educated—to signal their rejection of what they called "phoney" or "posh" artistic pretensions.
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: Aristocratic background and elite salons...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. This describes the **Bloomsbury Group** (e.g., Virginia Woolf), whom The Movement writers actively despised for their perceived elitism and "high-brow" aesthetic.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Working-class origins and radical activism...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. While they shared some "grumpy" energy with the working-class *Angry Young Men*, most Movement writers (like Larkin and Amis) were firmly **middle-class** and generally held skeptical, conservative, or moderate political views.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Cosmopolitan intellectual circles and experimental art...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The Movement was **anti-cosmopolitan** and **anti-experimental**. They preferred a local, traditional English focus over international modernism.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The "Plain Man" Aesthetic**: This was a deliberate cultural performance. By appearing as ordinary men who liked jazz, beer, and detective novels, they made poetry seem like a practical, "honest" craft rather than a mystical or elite calling.
 
• **Anti-Phoneyism**: A term popularized by the group (and J.D. Salinger around the same time) to describe their hatred for anything that seemed fake, overly sentimental, or intellectually arrogant.
 
• **Larkin and the Library**: Philip Larkin’s career as a librarian in Hull perfectly exemplified this "Movement" identity—working a steady, middle-class job in a provincial city while writing poetry that was technically masterful but grounded in everyday observation.

subject: ENG
question: Who coined the term 'The Movement'?

options.text: Kingsley Amis, one of the leading novelists of the group
J. D. Scott, literary editor of The Spectator
Donald Davie, poet-critic and member of the group
Robert Conquest, known for his satirical verses

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 2: J. D. Scott, literary editor of The Spectator.***

 
 
• The term **"The Movement"** was officially coined by **J. D. Scott** in an anonymous leading article titled **"In the Movement"** published in *The Spectator* on October 1, 1954.
 
• In the article, Scott identified a new group of British writers who shared a common skepticism toward the high-modernist and romantic styles of the previous decades.
 
• He described their work as being characterized by **"anti-phoneyism,"** technical proficiency, and a rejection of the "bloated" or "pretentious" language found in the works of Dylan Thomas or the Bloomsbury Group.
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: Kingsley Amis...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. While Amis was a central figure and his novel *Lucky Jim* (1954) is seen as a foundational text of the group, he did not name the movement himself.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Donald Davie...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. Davie was a key poet and critic associated with the group (especially through his work *Purity of Diction in English Verse*), but he was a participant rather than the coiner of the name.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: Robert Conquest...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. Conquest edited the famous anthology ***New Lines* (1956)**, which crystallized the group's identity, but J. D. Scott had already coined the term in the press two years earlier.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Historical Context**: The Movement emerged in the post-WWII era, reflecting a period of austerity and a shift toward the "Angry Young Men" sentiment in British culture.
 
• **Anti-Romanticism**: The group was largely defined by what they were *against*: the excessive emotion of Romanticism and the difficult, elitist obscurity of Modernism.
 
• **Key Contributors**: Along with Philip Larkin and Kingsley Amis, the group included John Wain, Elizabeth Jennings, Thom Gunn, and D. J. Enright. Their work often featured **irony**, **common sense**, and **traditional verse forms**.

subject: ENG
question: What attitude did The Movement writers share toward modernist literature?

options.text: They appreciated its intricacy and sought to experiment likewise through their writing.
They looked down upon its elitist nature and cultural pretensions, choosing clarity and accessibility in writing
They accepted the use of avant-garde techniques and denounced the English identity based on tradition.
They turned away from irony and nostalgia, concentrating exclusively on abstract philosophical discussions

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 2: They looked down upon its elitist nature and cultural pretensions, choosing clarity and accessibility in writing.***

 
 
• **The Movement** writers (such as Philip Larkin and Kingsley Amis) were defined by their reaction **against** the "difficulty" and obscurity of High Modernism (represented by T.S. Eliot and Ezra Pound).
 
• They felt that Modernism had become too **elitist** and disconnected from the ordinary reader. In response, they championed **"anti-phoneyism"**—a rejection of anything that seemed intellectually arrogant or overly complex.
 
• They prioritized **clarity**, **logic**, and **accessibility**, believing that literature should be grounded in the observable world rather than in abstract myths or private symbols.
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: They appreciated its intricacy and sought to experiment...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The group viewed Modernist experimentation as a "dead end" and preferred to return to **traditional English verse forms** like the sonnet or quatrain.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: They accepted the use of avant-garde techniques...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. They were famously suspicious of the **avant-garde**, which they associated with foreign (non-English) influences that they felt didn't fit the British temperament.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: They turned away from irony and nostalgia...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. Irony and a certain gritty nostalgia for a passing version of England were actually **central** to their style. They avoided "abstract philosophical discussions" in favor of concrete, everyday details.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rationalism over Romanticism**: The Movement writers valued the intellect over the "wild" emotions of the Romantics and the "stream-of-consciousness" confusion of the Modernists.
 
• **The "Grammar School" Poets**: Because many of them were educated in provincial grammar schools rather than the aristocratic circles of the Bloomsbury Group, their attitude toward Modernism was one of **middle-class skepticism** toward "high-brow" culture.
 
• **Philip Larkin's Prefaces**: Larkin often wrote about how he wanted poetry to be something people actually *wanted* to read, famously stating that he had no interest in "any poetry that requires a notebook of cross-references to understand."

• To choose the correct verb form, we must identify the **Subject** of the sentence and the **Tense** used in the passage.

• **Option 4:** **"Grapples"** is the singular form of the verb. It would be correct if the subject were "A scientist" (singular), but not for "Scientists."

question:
Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.

"Startups ______ a cultural shift from job seekers to job creators by fostering entrepreneurial opportunities nationwide."
solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 2: drive***

 
 
• The subject of the sentence is **"Startups"**, which is a **plural noun**.
 
• According to the rules of **subject-verb agreement**, a plural subject requires a plural verb (the base form of the verb without an 's').
 
• Since the sentence describes a general fact or ongoing state in the present tense, **"drive"** is the correct form to match the plural subject.
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: drives***
 
 
• This is **incorrect** because "drives" is the third-person singular form. It would be correct if the subject were singular (e.g., "The **startup drives** change").
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: driving***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. A present participle (ending in -ing) cannot function as the main verb of a sentence on its own; it requires an auxiliary verb like "are" (e.g., "Startups **are driving** a shift").
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: driven***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. "Driven" is a past participle and needs a helping verb to form a complete thought (e.g., "Startups **have driven** a shift" or "A shift **is driven** by startups").
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement Rule**: In the present tense, most verbs only change their ending for the third-person singular (he/she/it). For plural subjects (they), the verb remains in its base form.
 
• **Vocabulary Note**: In this context, to **"drive"** a shift means to be the primary cause or force behind a significant change in behavior or mindset within a society.

question:
Rewrite the sentence in passive voice.

“Governments emphasize strict traffic laws.”

options.text: Strict traffic laws are emphasized by governments.
Governments are emphasized by strict traffic laws.
Governments were emphasizing strict traffic laws.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Passive voice structure:** The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence. The formula for the present simple passive is: **Subject (Receiver) + am/is/are + Past Participle (V3) + by + Agent (Doer).**
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: *"Governments emphasize strict traffic laws."*
 
• **Step 1:** Identify the object, "strict traffic laws," and move it to the beginning of the sentence.
 
• **Step 2:** Change the active verb "emphasize" (present simple) to its passive form "are emphasized" to match the plural subject.
 
• **Step 3:** Place the original subject "Governments" at the end, introduced by the preposition "by."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Strict traffic laws are emphasized by governments."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: ***"Governments are emphasized by strict traffic laws."* – This incorrectly makes "Governments" the receiver of the action, reversing the logical meaning of the sentence.
 
• **Option 3: ***"Governments were emphasizing strict traffic laws."* – This is the **past continuous** tense in the **active voice**.
 
• **Option 4: ***"Strict traffic laws emphasize governments."* – This is an **active voice** sentence where the subject and object have been swapped, resulting in a nonsensical statement.

question: What is the claim of post-structuralism concerning the text?

options.text: The text is not tied to the author, with the reader being able to come up with several interpretations
The meaning of a text is constant and completely controlled by what the author intended.
A text is always a historical document, and subjective reading is not allowed.

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Independence from Authorial Intent.***

 
 
• The passage explains that "The Death of the Author" asserts the "independence of the literary text." It argues that a work is immune to being limited or unified by what the author originally intended or "crafted" into it.
 
 
 
• ***Radical Textual Independence.***
 
 
• Post-structuralism declares that a text is not determined by its context or the creator's intention. Instead, the text is "free by its very nature" from these restraints, allowing it to exist as a site of multiple meanings.
 
 
 
• ***Rejection of Fixed Meaning.***
 
 
• By moving away from "detailed, methodological" structuralism toward a style that emphasizes "randomness," Barthes suggests that a text cannot be pinned down to a single, stable interpretation.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2**: Incorrect because the passage states that the text is "immune" to being limited by authorial intent, directly contradicting the idea of a "controlled" meaning.
 
• **Option 3**: Incorrect because the passage explicitly notes that the work is "not determined by intention or context," and it emphasizes freedom and randomness rather than rigid historical documentation.
 
• **Option 4**: Incorrect because the "Death of the Author" specifically moves the focus away from the author's private life or biography as a source of meaning.

__
 
• **Active Voice structure:** In an active voice sentence, the subject is the "doer" of the action. The basic formula is: **Subject + Verb + Object.**
 
• In the sentence: *"Scammers design fake job postings to exploit job seekers."*
 
• **Subject:** "Scammers" (The entity performing the action).
 
• **Verb:** "design" (The action being performed).
 
• **Object:** "fake job postings" (The entity receiving the action).
 
• Since the subject ("Scammers") is directly performing the action of "designing," the sentence is in the **Active Voice**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Active Sentence:** *"Scammers design fake job postings to exploit job seekers."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: Passive Voice** – In the passive voice, the object becomes the subject: *"Fake job postings **are designed** by scammers to exploit job seekers."*
 
• **Option 3: Reflexive Voice** – This occurs when the subject and the object are the same person or thing (e.g., *"The scammers **disguised themselves**."*).
 
• **Option 4: Causative Voice** – This indicates that the subject causes someone else to do something (e.g., *"The leader **had the scammers design** fake postings."*).

subject: ENG
question: In what ways did Wollstonecraft’s feminist approach stand in contrast to that of Marxist-feminist thinkers?

options.text: She limited her examination to economic equality, neglecting the cultural and social side of gender discrimination
She maintained that class struggle was a more important factor than gender equity in the pursuit of social justice
She regarded patriarchy as an illusion and considered women to be instinctively suited for the home
She highlighted the importance of motherhood in society's development, which wasn’t considered by Marxist feminists

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 4: She highlighted the importance of motherhood in society's development, which wasn’t considered by Marxist feminists.***

 
 
• The passage explicitly identifies this point of contention in the final sentence: **"Her idea, that women play a crucial role in shaping a society through their participation in bringing up children, was downrightly rejected by the Marxist-feminist thinkers."**
 
• Wollstonecraft argued that motherhood was a vital social office that required a rational education to perform correctly, whereas Marxist-feminists often focused on how domestic labor serves the capitalist economy.
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: She limited her examination to economic equality...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. Wollstonecraft's work focused primarily on **education and social/political rights**. It is actually the Marxist-feminists who center their analysis on the economic structures of society.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: She maintained that class struggle was a more important factor...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. Class struggle is the defining characteristic of **Marxist** theory. Wollstonecraft's approach is considered "proto-feminist" or "liberal feminist," focusing on individual rights and equality under the law.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: She regarded patriarchy as an illusion...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage states that her work **"critiques the position of women in a patriarchal set-up,"** meaning she recognized it as a very real and harmful social structure.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Liberal Feminism (Wollstonecraft's path)**: Focuses on achieving gender equality through political and legal reform within the framework of a liberal democracy. It emphasizes **education** and **individual agency**.
 
• **Marxist Feminism**: Argues that women's oppression is tied to the system of capitalism and private property. They believe true liberation can only happen by dismantling the capitalist system.
 
• **Proto-feminist**: This term is used for thinkers like Wollstonecraft who wrote before the feminist movement was "named," but whose ideas laid the groundwork for modern gender equality.

subject: ENG
question: Why did Brecht's plays gain recognition in the West only in the mid-20th century?

options.text: The audiences started to reject the realism of Stanislavsky and the well-made plays and looked for new theatrical forms.
Brecht changed his style and began writing romantic dramas, which were easier to digest by the public.
An explanation for this is that his plays were not allowed in Europe until the end of World War II.
Another reason for this is that he deserted political matters and solely concentrated on entertainment.

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 1: The audiences started to reject the realism of Stanislavsky and the well-made plays and looked for new theatrical forms.***

 
 
• The passage explicitly states that Brecht's plays gained recognition in the mid-20th century **"when people began rejecting Stanislavsky-oriented realism and the presentation of Well-made plays on stage."**
 
• This shift in audience preference away from traditional, immersive realism allowed the more analytical and "instructive" style of **Epic Theatre** to become popular.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Brecht changed his style and began writing romantic dramas...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The text defines Brecht's work as **"Epic theatre,"** which is **"instructive"** and uses the **"alienation effect"** rather than romantic or emotional empathy.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: ...his plays were not allowed in Europe until the end of World War II.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. While historically true in some contexts, this information is **not mentioned** in the provided passage, which focuses on theatrical theory and audience taste.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: ...he deserted political matters and solely concentrated on entertainment.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage describes his theatre as having **"analysis, argument, or evidence"** and being **"didactic,"** which indicates a focus on intellectual and often political instruction rather than pure entertainment.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stanislavsky-oriented Realism**: A style of theatre that aims for total "illusion," where the audience feels they are watching "real life" and empathizes deeply with characters' emotions.
 
• **Alienation Effect (Verfremdungseffekt)**: A technique used by Brecht to "make the familiar strange." By breaking the theatrical illusion, he forced the audience to remain **objective observers** so they could think critically about the play's message.
 
• **Well-made Play**: A 19th-century genre of theatre characterized by a very tight, logical plot and a climax that resolves all conflicts—the very thing Brecht's loosely knit "episodic structure" rejected.
 
• **Chinese Theatre Influence**: Brecht admired how Chinese actors appeared to observe their own performance from the outside, helping to maintain the distance necessary for the alienation effect.

subject: ENG
question: **Why does the passage state that “no machine can replace human responsibility” even though future cars will be safer and more intelligent?**

options.text: Because machines are not allowed on all roads
Because pedestrians will not follow rules
Because machines cannot make ethical decisions and drivers must remain alert

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Limitations in Ethical Reasoning.***

 
 
• While AI and intelligent systems can process data faster than humans, they lack the capacity for moral judgment. In complex, split-second "life-or-death" scenarios, machines follow programmed logic rather than understanding the ethical weight of their actions.
 
 
 
• ***The Necessity of Human Oversight.***
 
 
• "Responsibility" implies accountability. Because a machine cannot be held legally or morally liable in the same way a person can, a human driver must remain alert to intervene and take control when the technology encounters an unpredictable situation.
 
 
 
• ***Unpredictability of the Environment.***
 
 
• Even a "safer" car cannot account for every possible external variable. The phrase emphasizes that technology is a tool to assist, but the ultimate duty of care remains with the human operator to ensure safety for everyone on the road.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: Incorrect because the legal status of machines on roads is a matter of regulation, not an explanation for the fundamental nature of "human responsibility."
 
• **Option 2**: Incorrect because the premise of the question states that future cars will be safer, contradicting the idea that technology is "always" unsafe.
 
• **Option 3**: Incorrect because while pedestrian behavior is a challenge, "human responsibility" specifically refers to the person operating the vehicle, not the behavior of others.

subject: ENG
question: Why is “The Death of the Author” seen as the turning point in Barthes’s intellectual journey?

options.text: Due to its introduction of a new type of biography that placed emphasis on the psychological history of the authors
By implication, it recommended that the authors stay away from their personal lives as a source of inspiration for their works
In this sense, it was the cause of the authors being pushed towards unveiling their creative workings through their writing
Through the symbolic act of virtually saying that texts shouldn't be linked to the authors' intentions, thus granting radical freedom to texts

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***The "Hinge" of Intellectual Shift.***

 
 
• The passage describes the 1968 essay as the "hinge" around which Barthes turns from the rigid, technical methods of structuralism to the more fluid ideas of post-structuralism.
 
 
 
• ***Assertion of Textual Independence.***
 
 
• By "announcing the death of the author," Barthes is using a rhetorical device to argue that a literary work is independent and "immune" to being limited by the author's personal biography or original intent.
 
 
 
• ***Granting Radical Freedom.***
 
 
• The essay serves as a "declaration of radical textual independence," suggesting that the text's meaning is not fixed by its context or creator but is free by its very nature from all such restraints.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: Incorrect because the essay explicitly rejects the importance of an author's "psychological history" or biography in favor of the text itself.
 
• **Option 2**: Incorrect because the essay is a theory of criticism and reading, not a set of practical recommendations for how authors should live their personal lives.
 
• **Option 3**: Incorrect because the goal of the essay was to separate the text from the author's "creative workings" or intentions, rather than pushing authors to unveil them.

subject: ENG
question: The Pleasure of the Text is viewed as a post-structuralist text for the following reasons:

options.text: It does not provide a strict, linear analysis of narrative systems but rather presents them in a very fragmented manner that is confusing for the readers
It claims that only scholars are qualified to ascertain the correct interpretation of a work.
The narrative is explained scientifically through the use of models and statistics.
By rejecting strict methodology, the author provides random, alphabetically organized thoughts, which reveal the text's unpredictability.

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Rejection of Technical Methodology.***

 
 
• The passage contrasts *The Pleasure of the Text* with Barthes's earlier structuralist work, which was "detailed, methodological, and forbiddingly technical." By moving away from this rigid system, the text aligns with post-structuralist values of fluidity.
 
 
 
• ***Alphabetical and Random Organization.***
 
 
• The work is described as a "series of random comments on narrative, arranged alphabetically." This deliberate choice of structure serves to emphasize the "randomness of the material" rather than a forced, unified logic.
 
 
 
• ***Embracing Unpredictability.***
 
 
• By organizing the text in this way, Barthes demonstrates the "radical textual independence" mentioned in the passage. It shows that the text is free from the restraints of a pre-determined "crafted" order, highlighting its inherent unpredictability.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: Incorrect because while the text is fragmented, the passage focuses on the "alphabetical arrangement" and "randomness" as the defining post-structuralist features rather than a goal to "confuse" the reader.
 
• **Option 2**: Incorrect because post-structuralism, through the "Death of the Author," actually democratizes the text, moving away from the idea that any single figure (author or scholar) has the exclusive "correct" interpretation.
 
• **Option 3**: Incorrect because the use of "models and statistics" is characteristic of Barthes's earlier structuralist phase, which the passage describes as "methodological" and "technical."

subject: ENG
question: Why does the poet describe a sense of loneliness in the poem?

options.text: As he is going through a dry creative period, even though he is in the middle of a crowd.
As he is literally pushed away in a forest far from any human being.
As he considers himself an outsider to the social group and does not want to interact with anyone at all.
As he remembers the good old days of his childhood, he longs for the countryside life very much.

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 1: As he is going through a dry creative period, even though he is in the middle of a crowd.***

 
 
• The passage explicitly clarifies the nature of the poet's isolation: **"this loneliness is not the absence of people around him, but the absence of Creative powers."**
 
• A "dry creative period" is a common literary way to describe the **absence of inspiration** or "Creative powers" mentioned in the text. Even if people are physically present, the poet feels "lonely" because he cannot connect with his own imagination.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: As he is literally pushed away in a forest far from any human being.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage states that the fox is an **image** or **symbol** and that the loneliness is specifically *not* about the physical absence of people.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: As he considers himself an outsider to the social group...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The text focuses entirely on the **process of poetic inspiration** and the "blank pages," rather than the poet's social standing or his desire to interact with others.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: As he remembers the good old days of his childhood...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. There is no mention of childhood, nostalgia, or a longing for the countryside life in the provided passage.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Writer's Block**: The phrase "his fingers move, but the pages remain blank" is a classic description of writer's block. The "loneliness" here is the frustration of having the tools to write but lacking the internal "spark."
 
• **Symbolic Fox**: The fox is the **thought** that gradually becomes solid. Just as a fox's nose or eyes might appear first in the darkness of a forest, a poem often begins with a single, small image or "part" before the whole idea is formed.
 
• **Loneliness as a Catalyst**: For many poets, this "special kind of loneliness" is necessary for the imagination to take shape, as it forces the mind to look inward for the "fox" to appear.

subject: ENG
question: What is the idea that best reflects the attitude of the passage with respect to the needs of mentally healthy individuals, which would involve things such as security, relationships, and a sense of accomplishment?

options.text: These are different from mental health and should be considered individually.
Only security needs have the ability to impact mental health.
The needs are considered irrelevant within a psychological framework that deals with long-term psychological distress.
These needs are interconnected and must be addressed alongside emotional and existential suffering.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To identify the passage's attitude toward these needs, we look at the final sentence: *"...care as the task of addressing adverse life circumstances... **while at the same time addressing needs related to security, relationship, daily accomplishment, or problem-solving**, is a very complicated story."*
 
• The use of the phrase **"while at the same time"** indicates that these practical and social needs (security, relationships, accomplishment) are not separate from mental health care but are **interconnected** with it.
 
• The "radical vision" described doesn't choose between fixing life circumstances and fixing the mind; it advocates for addressing **both** simultaneously.
 
• **Option 4** perfectly reflects this holistic attitude by stating these needs must be addressed **alongside** emotional and existential suffering.
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 1:** The passage suggests they should be addressed "at the same time," which is the opposite of considering them "individually" or as "different from mental health."
 
• **Option 2:** This is **too restrictive**. The passage also mentions relationships, daily accomplishment, and problem-solving, not just security.
 
• **Option 3:** This **contradicts** the text, which explicitly includes these needs as part of the "task of care" in its complicated story.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **4**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In high-level Reading Comprehension, look for "Integrative" keywords like "while," "simultaneously," or "at the same time." These words signal that the author views various elements as a **unified whole** rather than isolated parts.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Existential Issues:** Philosophical concerns about the meaning of life, purpose, and death.
 
• **Disability Justice:** A movement that ensures people with disabilities have the same rights and opportunities as everyone else, with a focus on intersectionality.
 
• **Equity:** Ensuring everyone has the specific tools they need to be successful, which is different from "equality" (giving everyone the same thing).
 
• **Adverse:** Unfavorable or harmful circumstances.

• Third conditional sentence is used to explain that present situation would be different if something different had happened in the past.
 
• The incident that happens first or was supposed to happen first takes a past perfect tense **(had + V3 form of verb)** in the ‘If’ clause when **‘would/should/could have’ **is present in the main clause that expresses the hypothetical situation that could have happened.
 
• In the question, ‘If I had known about him before’ is the incident that is supposed to happen first. Therefore, ‘would have recommended’ (had + V3 form of verb) should be the correct verb form used here.

Therefore, the corrected sentence is: "*If I had known about him before, I **would have **recommended him."*

subject: ENG
question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

Mr. Roy was not only very successful and humble also.
solution:
The erroneous part is **'and humble also'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of **correlative conjunction** since it has **not only** in the first clause.
 
• Correlative conjunctions are a **pair of words **that connect **similar entities**(nouns, adjectives, etc) in the sentence **together**.
 
• It is used to put emphasis on certain elements.
 
• Common examples of correlative conjunctions include **either or, neither nor, not only but also, both and**.

**Hence the correct sentence is**__: *Mr. Roy was not only very successful __**but also **__humble*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• Correlative conjunction is also known to maintain the grammatical balance in a sentence.
 
• it can only connect two similar entities together. Like if the first clause of the sentence had a noun then it will be connected to another noun in the second clause of the sentence.
 
 
• Example: **Both** India **and **China have huge populations. (**nouns**)
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 
• It is really easy to get confused about which conjunction to use in a particular sentence.
 
• If the first clause of the statement is similar to the second clause then we can use coordinating conjunction like **and**.
 
 
• **Example**: *He was handsome **and **talented as well*.
 
 
 
• If the first clause of the statement is in stark contrast to the second clause of the statement then we use **but.**
 
 
• **Example: ***He was talented **but **lacked discipline.*
 
 
 
• There is no need to use commas in case two nouns are connected through conjunction but in other sentences a comma is necessary.
 
 
• **Example**: The restaurant owner not only offered us a free lunch, but he also gave us a complimentary beverage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Replace "**being**" with "**be**" to correct the sentence.
 
• "**Be**" is the infinitive. It means to exist or to take place. It’s an irregular verb.
 
• "**Be**" is used in commands and with modals. ('can' in this sentence)
 
• We use modal verbs to talk about things like a possibility, ability, and obligation, or to make a request or a suggestion.
 
• In the present tense, we always use modal verbs with base verbs.
 
• So, when we use "**be**" with modal verbs like can, could, will, would, must, or should to name a few, we don’t have to change it. 
 
• The word '**being**' is the present participle form of the verb 'be'. It is used only with continuous tenses.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**, which contains an error.

solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: **Neither she not I**

• Replace "**not**" with "**nor**" to correct the sentence.
 
• We can use neither as a conjunction with nor. It connects two or more negative alternatives. It is called correlative conjunction.
 
• **Correlative conjunctions** are conjunctions used to illustrate how two words or phrases within a sentence relate to each other.
 
• Correlative conjunctions always come in pairs. (either/or, neither/nor)
 
• '**Neither/nor**' is used when two options are invalid.
 
• In the given sentence it is said that, she and I are not participating in the debate tournament. (both are negative)
 
• We use "**nor**" before the second or farther of two alternatives when "**neither**" introduces the first.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**, which contains the error.

**Corrected sentence:** *Neither she nor I am going to take part in the debate competition.*

Foods turn brown and crispy when we cook them because for chemical reactions.
solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: **because for chemical reactions**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error here lies in the use of prepositions.
 
• Replace "**for**" with "**of**" to correct the sentence.
 
• We use '**for**' to talk about a purpose or a reason for something.
 
• '**Of**' is a preposition that indicates relationships between other words, such as belonging, things made of other things, things that contain other things, or a point of reckoning.
 
• "**Because of**" is a preposition comprising two words. It is usually used before a noun, gerund or a pronoun.
 
• "A because of B" means B caused A to happen.
 
 
• **For example-** *Ram was late this morning because of the heavy traffic.*
 
 
 
• From here we can say that "**because of**" should be used here.
 
• Hence, **option 3** is the correct answer which contains an error in it.

**Corrected sentence:** *Foods turn brown and crispy when we cook them because of__ chemical reactions.*

• The error is in the use of **an**, instead of 'an' it should be **'a'.**
 
• 'A' is used when the next noun or adjective is starting with the sound of consonant while "An" is used when the next noun or adjective is starting with the sound of vowel.
 
• **Example **- an apple, a man, an orange, a dog.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• There are two types of articles :** Definite articles and Indefinite articles.**
 
• The** definite article (the)** is used before a noun to indicate that the reader is aware of the noun's identity.
 
• The **indefinite article (a, an)** is used before a general noun or when the identity of the noun is unknown. In some cases, a noun does not require an article.

 ** Example**: He was **finished** with the project.

Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

If your kids sleep well, they are likely to behave better.
solution:
The correct answer is 'No error'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically correct and there are no errors in its syntax, vocabulary, or structure.
 
• The sentence is in the present tense, and it conveys a simple cause-and-effect relationship. It states that if kids sleep well, they are likely to behave better.
 
• 
 
**Let's analyze the given sentence and explain the correctness of each part based on grammar rules and syntax.**

 
 
• 
 
***The sentence is: "If your kids sleep well, they are likely to behave better."***

 
 
• 
 
"If your kids sleep well": This is a conditional clause that starts with the subordinating conjunction "if." In English grammar, a conditional clause typically consists of an "if" or "unless" clause followed by a main clause. In this case, "If your kids sleep well" is the conditional clause, and it is grammatically correct.

 
 
• 
 
"they are likely": This is the main clause of the sentence, and it follows the conditional clause. The subject "they" refers to "your kids," and the verb "are likely" indicates the probability or likelihood of a certain outcome. Grammatically, there is no error in this part.

 
 
• 
 
"to behave better": This is an infinitive phrase that acts as the complement to the verb "are likely." Infinitive phrases often function as noun phrases, adjectives, or adverbs in a sentence. In this case, "to behave better" acts as an adverbial phrase modifying the verb "are likely." It answers the question "in what way are they likely?" and indicates that the likelihood is tied to their behavior. This part is also grammatically correct.

 
 
• 
 
Therefore, the answer is "No error."

 
 
• Correct sentence__: If your kids sleep well, they are likely to behave better.

• The word "diligent" is an adjective.
 
• We need an adverb form of the word "diligent" to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• An adverb is a word that modifies (describes) a verb (he sings loudly), an adjective (very tall), another adverb (ended too quickly), or even a whole sentence.
 
• Adverbs often end in -ly, but some (such as fast) look exactly the same as their adjective counterparts. 
 
• The adverb form of "diligent" is "diligently."
 
• Therefore, the use of 'diligent' should be replaced with 'diligently' to modify the verb "dig" to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• So, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 ​

• The error is in subject-verb agreement.
 
• The phrase "**far, far at the top of them**" is not a complete sentence and lacks a subject and verb.
 
• In the sentence "Far, far at the top of them, a shower of bright red sparks had flared among the stars," **the subject is "a shower,**" which is a **singular noun**.
 
• However, the pronoun "them" is used, which is plural. This creates a mismatch in number agreement.
 
• In English grammar, subject-verb agreement means that the subject (the noun or pronoun that the sentence is about) must agree in number with the verb (the action word).
 
• If the subject is singular, the verb should be singular; if the subject is plural, the verb should be plural.
 
• In this case, the singular pronoun "**it**" should be used instead of "them."
 
• **The corrected sentence is**: "*Far, far at the top of it, a shower of bright red sparks had flared among the stars.*"

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

They had been dancing / for an hour / when our dance teacher / had arrived.
solution:
The correct answer is: **had arrived**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence uses the** past perfect continuous tense** ("had been dancing") to describe an action that was ongoing in the past.
 
• The phrase "when our dance teacher had arrived" incorrectly uses the past perfect tense ("had arrived") instead of the **simple past tense**.
 
• The correct phrase should be "when our dance teacher arrived" to indicate that the arrival of the dance teacher interrupted the ongoing action of dancing.
 
• The sentence contains two clauses: the main clause and the subordinate (dependent) clause.
 
 
• Main clause: "They had been dancing for an hour"
 
• Subordinate clause: "when our dance teacher arrived"
 
 
 
• The use of the **past simple tense** in the **subordinate clause** (arrived) is essential because it marks the specific point in time at which the ongoing action (dancing) met an interruption or new event.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Correct sentence: *They had been dancing for an hour when our dance teacher arrived.*

__
 
• The phrase 'The cholera' is incorrect in this context.
 
• **Cholera is an uncountable noun and does not require an article ('the') in this context.**
 
• In English, diseases are typically** not preceded by the definite article 'the'.**
 
 
• **Example:** Correct: Cholera is a frightful disease. Incorrect: The cholera is a frightful disease.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: ***Cholera **is a frightful disease.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Articles ('a', 'an', 'the') are generally not used with uncountable nouns (like diseases, ideas, etc.).
 
 
• **Example:** Happiness is essential for a healthy life.
 
 
 
• When referring to specific, well-known entities or unique items, 'the' is appropriate.
 
 
• **Example:** The Sun rises in the East.
 
 
 
• Common countable nouns require articles depending on their definiteness.
 
 
• **Example:** A cat sits on the roof.

question: Select the option that has an error in the use of present tense.

options.text: The painter is painting the wall right now.
The mother cooks delicious food for her children.
I am observing your mischievous activities for half an hour.
I have performed all my duties with utmost sincerity.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence "**I am observing your mischievous activities for half an hour**" contains an error in the use of present continuous tense.
 
• The present continuous tense is used to describe actions happening **right now** or around the current time. However, it should not be used for an action that started in the past and continues for a specific period of time unless it is indicated with a duration or completion.
 
• To express an action that has been happening for a period of time, the **present perfect continuous** tense should be used instead: "**I have been observing your mischievous activities for half an hour**."
 
• Other options are grammatically correct: 
 
 
• **Option 1:** The use of present continuous tense is correct, indicating an action happening right now.
 
• **Option 2:** Simple present tense is correctly used to describe a regular action.
 
• **Option 4:** Present perfect tense is correctly used to describe an action completed in the past with relevance to the present.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I **have been observing** your mischievous activities for half an hour."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Present Continuous Tense** is used for actions happening **at this moment** (e.g., "I am eating dinner right now").
 
• **Present Perfect Continuous Tense** is used for actions that began in the past and are still continuing (e.g., "I have been working all day").
